In its quarterly earnings, Apple reported that R&D spending climbed to a record $11.73 billion, continuing a trend of sharply accelerating expenditure throughout fiscal year 2026. Details below.

Apple Increases R&D Spending

Apple reported R&D spending of $11.4 billion last quarter, a year-over-year increase of 34%.

On Apple's earnings call, Tim Cook said the company is "clearly investing more" and noted that R&D spending is "accelerating at a much higher rate than the company overall."

He went on to reiterate that R&D spending has "significantly scaled up on a year-over-year basis," particularly when discussing Apple's AI investments. Apple CFO Kevan Parekh added that AI-related spending is being layered on top of Apple's normal product roadmap investments.

Apple reported record R&D spending of $11.73 billion for the third quarter of 2026 today, up 32% from a year earlier, bringing Apple's cumulative R&D expenditure in fiscal year 2026 to $34.04 billion.

For comparison, Apple spent $34.55 billion on R&D across all of fiscal year 2025. That means with one quarter still remaining, the company has nearly matched last year's full-year total, while already surpassing the full-year R&D spending of fiscal years 2024 and 2023.

Over the past few days, Wall Street has punished companies that announced accelerating AI-related spending without demonstrating equally clear near-term returns.

Alphabet's stock fell 7% after it raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $15 billion to between $195 billion and $205 billion. Meta's stock also dropped roughly 9% to 10% after reporting a 91% plunge in free cash flow and raising the lower end of its annual capex forecast to $130 billion.

Apple shares are currently down about 4% in after-hours trading. This reaction may change during the earnings call and will fluctuate again during normal trading hours tomorrow.
